nodes.name: Prolate spheroidal wave functions (PSWFs)
nodes.genus: the solutions of the following energy maximization problem
nodes.statement_short: PSWFs are the band-limited functions maximizing the energy concentration on $[-1,1]$.

nodes.name: Paley-Wiener space $B_c$
Paley-Wiener space $B_c$
nodes.statement: B_c=\{ f\in L^2(\mathbb R),\,\, \mbox{Support } \widehat f\subseteq [-c,c]\}.
nodes.label: Bc

nodes.name: Fourier transform
nodes.statement: Here, $\widehat f$ is the Fourier transform of $f\in L^2(\mathbb R),$ defined by ${\displaystyle \widehat f(\xi)=\lim_{A\rightarrow +\infty}\int_{[-A,A]} e^{-i x\xi} f(x)\, dx.}$

nodes.name: PSWFs as eigenfunctions of the sinc-kernel operator and commuting differential operator
nodes.statement:
Moreover, it has been shown in \cite{Slepian1},  that the PSWFs are also the eigenfunctions of the integral operator ${\displaystyle \mathcal Q_c}$ defined on $L^2(-1,1)$ by $${\displaystyle \mathcal Q_c f(x)=\int_{-1}^1 \frac{\sin(c(x-y))}{\pi(x-y)} f(y)\, dy} $$ as well as the eigenfunctions of a  commuting differential operator $ \mathcal{L}_c$ with $ \mathcal{Q}_c$ and given by
$$ \mathcal L_c f(x)= (1-x^2)f''(x)-2x f'(x) - c^2 x^2 f(x) $$
nodes.statement_short: PSWFs are eigenfunctions of the sinc-kernel integral operator $\mathcal Q_c$ and of the commuting differential operator $\mathcal L_c$.
conclusions: the PSWFs are also the eigenfunctions of the integral operator ${\displaystyle \mathcal Q_c}$

nodes.name: Generalized prolate spheroidal wave functions (GPSWFs)
nodes.statement_short: GPSWFs are the eigenfunctions of the Gegenbauer-perturbed differential operator and of the weighted finite Fourier transform $\mathcal F_c^{(\alpha)}$.

nodes.name: Weighted finite Fourier transform operator
nodes.statement: {\displaystyle \mathcal F_c^{(\alpha)} f(x)=\int_{-1}^1 e^{icxy} f(y)\,(1-y^2)^{\alpha}\, dy,\, \alpha > -1.}
nodes.label: integraloperator

nodes.name: GPSWF projection $S_N$
nodes.statement: In this work, we further study the convergence rate of the projection ${\displaystyle S_N \cdot f = \displaystyle \sum_{k=0}^N <f,\psi_{n,c}^{(\alpha)}> \psi_{n,c}^{(\alpha)} }$ to $f$ .
nodes.statement_short: $S_N f$ is the truncated GPSWF series expansion (orthogonal projection) of $f$.

nodes.name: Jacobi weight $\omega_\alpha$ and weighted norm
nodes.statement: Here $$ \omega_\alpha(t) = (1-t^2)^{\alpha} \mbox{ and } \norm{.}_{\omega} = \norm{.}_{L^2(I,\omega_\alpha)} $$

nodes.name: Theorem 1 (approximation by GPSWFs in weighted Sobolev spaces, announced)
nodes.statement: Let $c>1$ and $\alpha >0$, then there exist constants $K>0$ and $a>0$ such that, when $N > m_{\alpha}c$ with $m_{\alpha}=4.13\left(1.28+\frac{2\alpha+1}{1.9}\right)^{0.55}$ and $f \in H^s_{\alpha}$; $s > 0$, we have the inequality \begin{eqnarray} \|f-S_N(f)\|_{L^2(I, \omega_{\alpha})} &\leq& \left(1+ \left(\frac{N}{2}\right)^2\right)^{\frac{-s}{2}} \|f\|_{H^s_{\alpha}} +K.e^{-a N}\|f\|_{L^2(I,\omega_{\alpha})} \end{eqnarray} Where $S_N(f)(t)=\displaystyle{\sum_{n<N}}<f,\psi_{n,c}^{\alpha}>_{L^2_{\alpha}(I)}\psi_{n,c}^{\alpha}$
nodes.statement_short: For $N>m_\alpha c$, the GPSWF truncation error of $f\in H^s_\alpha$ is $O((1+N^2/4)^{-s/2})\|f\|_{H^s_\alpha}$ plus an exponentially small term.
conclusions: there exist constants $K>0$ and $a>0$ such that

nodes.name: Weighted Sobolev approximation bound (announced)
nodes.statement: \|f-S_N(f)\|_{L^2(I, \omega_{\alpha})} &\leq& \left(1+ \left(\frac{N}{2}\right)^2\right)^{\frac{-s}{2}} \|f\|_{H^s_{\alpha}} +K.e^{-a N}\|f\|_{L^2(I,\omega_{\alpha})}
nodes.label: ineq

nodes.name: Eigenvalues $\lambda_n^{(\alpha)}(c)$, $\mu_n^{(\alpha)}(c)$ and operator $\mathcal Q_c^{(\alpha)}$
nodes.statement:
Our study of the convergence rate of $ \norm{S_N-Id}$ is done by using an estimate for the  decay of the eigenvalues $\lambda^{(\alpha)}_n(c)$ of the self-adjoint  operator ${\displaystyle \mathcal Q_c^{(\alpha)} =\frac{c}{2\pi}  \mathcal F_c^{(\alpha)^*} \mathcal F_c^{(\alpha)},}$ that is
$ \lambda_n^{(\alpha)}(c) = \frac{c}{2\pi}{|\mu_n^{(\alpha)}(c)|^2}$, where   $\mu_n^{(\alpha)}$ is the n-th eigenvalues of the integral operator given by \eqref{integraloperator}.
nodes.statement_short: $\lambda_n^{(\alpha)}(c)=\frac{c}{2\pi}|\mu_n^{(\alpha)}(c)|^2$ are the eigenvalues of $\mathcal Q_c^{(\alpha)}=\frac{c}{2\pi}\mathcal F^*\mathcal F$, $\mu_n$ those of $\mathcal F_c^{(\alpha)}$.
also_stated_at:
Moreover, the eigenvalues $\mu_n^{(\alpha)}(c)$ and $\lambda_n^{(\alpha)}(c)$ of $\mathcal F_c^{(\alpha)}$ and
$\mathcal Q_c^{(\alpha)}$ are related to each others by the identity
${\displaystyle \lambda_n^{(\alpha)}(c)= \frac{c}{2\pi } |\mu_n^{(\alpha)}(c)|^2}.$

nodes.name: Super-exponential decay of the eigenvalues of the weighted finite Fourier transform
nodes.statement: For given real numbers $c > 0$,$ \;\; \;\alpha\geq 0$ and for any integer $n > \frac{ec+1}{2},$ we have \begin{equation} | \mu_n^{(\alpha)}(c)| \leq \frac{k_{\alpha}}{c^{\frac{\alpha}{2}+1}\log\left(\frac{2n-1}{ec}\right)} \left(\frac{ec}{2n-1}\right)^{n+\frac{\alpha}{2}},\;\;\; k_{\alpha}=\left(\frac{2}{e}\right)^{1+\frac{\alpha}{2}}\pi(\Gamma(\alpha+1))^{1/2}. \end{equation} and \begin{equation} \lambda_n^{(\alpha)}(c) \leq \frac{K_\alpha}{c^{\alpha+1}\log^2(\frac{2n-1}{ec})}\Big(\frac{ec}{2n-1}\Big)^{2n+\alpha} \quad \mbox{with} \quad K_{\alpha} = \frac{\pi}{2}\big(2/e \big)^{\alpha+2} \Gamma(\alpha+1)\nonumber \end{equation}
also_stated_at: For given real numbers $c > 0$,$ \;\; \;\alpha\geq 0$ and for any integer $n > \frac{ec+1}{2},$ we have \begin{equation} | \mu_n^{(\alpha)}(c)| \leq \frac{k_{\alpha}}{c^{\frac{\alpha}{2}+1}\log\left(\frac{2n-1}{ec}\right)} \left(\frac{ec}{2n-1}\right)^{n+\frac{\alpha}{2}},\;\;\; k_{\alpha}=\left(\frac{2}{e}\right)^{1+\frac{\alpha}{2}}\pi(\Gamma(\alpha+1))^{1/2}. \end{equation} and \begin{equation} \lambda_n^{(\alpha)}(c) \leq \frac{K_\alpha}{c^{\alpha+1}\log^2(\frac{2n-1}{ec})}\Big(\frac{ec}{2n-1}\Big)^{2n+\alpha} \quad \mbox{with} \quad K_{\alpha} = \frac{\pi}{2}\big(2/e \big)^{\alpha+2} \Gamma(\alpha+1) \end{equation}
nodes.statement_short: Explicit super-exponential bounds $|\mu_n|\lesssim (ec/(2n-1))^{n+\alpha/2}/\log(\cdot)$ and $\lambda_n\lesssim (ec/(2n-1))^{2n+\alpha}/\log^2(\cdot)$ for $n>(ec+1)/2$.

nodes.name: Decay bound for $|\mu_n^{(\alpha)}(c)|$
nodes.statement: | \mu_n^{(\alpha)}(c)| \leq \frac{k_{\alpha}}{c^{\frac{\alpha}{2}+1}\log\left(\frac{2n-1}{ec}\right)} \left(\frac{ec}{2n-1}\right)^{n+\frac{\alpha}{2}},\;\;\; k_{\alpha}=\left(\frac{2}{e}\right)^{1+\frac{\alpha}{2}}\pi(\Gamma(\alpha+1))^{1/2}.
nodes.label: Eq3.1

nodes.name: Decay bound for $\lambda_n^{(\alpha)}(c)$
nodes.statement: \lambda_n^{(\alpha)}(c) \leq \frac{K_\alpha}{c^{\alpha+1}\log^2(\frac{2n-1}{ec})}\Big(\frac{ec}{2n-1}\Big)^{2n+\alpha} \quad \mbox{with} \quad K_{\alpha} = \frac{\pi}{2}\big(2/e \big)^{\alpha+2} \Gamma(\alpha+1)\nonumber
nodes.label: newdecay

nodes.name: Weighted finite Fourier transform operator
nodes.statement:
The GPSWFs are defined as the eigenfunctions of
the weighted finite Fourier transform operator $\mathcal F_c^{(\alpha)},$ defined  by
\begin{equation} \mathcal F_c^{(\alpha)} f(x)=\int_{-1}^1 e^{icxy}  f(y)\,\omega_{\alpha}(y)\, dy,\quad \omega_{\alpha}(y)=(1-y^2)^{\alpha},\quad \alpha >0
\end{equation}

nodes.name: Weighted finite Fourier transform $\mathcal F_c^{(\alpha)}$
nodes.statement: \mathcal F_c^{(\alpha)} f(x)=\int_{-1}^1 e^{icxy} f(y)\,\omega_{\alpha}(y)\, dy,\quad \omega_{\alpha}(y)=(1-y^2)^{\alpha},\quad \alpha >0
nodes.label: Eq1.1

nodes.name: Operator $\mathcal Q_c^{(\alpha)}$ with Bessel kernel
nodes.statement:
They are also the eigenfunctions of the
operator ${\displaystyle \mathcal Q_c^{(\alpha)}=\frac{c}{2\pi}\mathcal F_c^{({\alpha})^*} \circ \mathcal F_c^{(\alpha)}},$   defined on $L^2{(I, \omega_{\alpha})}$ by
\begin{equation} \mathcal Q_c^{(\alpha)} g (x) = \int_{-1}^1 \frac{c}{2 \pi}\mathcal K_{\alpha}(c(x-y)) g(y) \omega_{\alpha}(y) \, dy,
\quad \mathcal K_{\alpha}(x)=\sqrt{\pi} 2^{\alpha+1/2}\Gamma(\alpha+1) \frac{J_{\alpha+1/2}(x)}{x^{\alpha+1/2}}.
\end{equation}
Here $ J_{\alpha}(\cdot)$ is the Bessel function of the first kind and order $ \alpha>-1.$

nodes.name: Integral form of $\mathcal Q_c^{(\alpha)}$
nodes.statement: \mathcal Q_c^{(\alpha)} g (x) = \int_{-1}^1 \frac{c}{2 \pi}\mathcal K_{\alpha}(c(x-y)) g(y) \omega_{\alpha}(y) \, dy, \quad \mathcal K_{\alpha}(x)=\sqrt{\pi} 2^{\alpha+1/2}\Gamma(\alpha+1) \frac{J_{\alpha+1/2}(x)}{x^{\alpha+1/2}}.
nodes.label: EEq0

nodes.name: Gegenbauer-type Sturm-Liouville operator $\mathcal L_c^{(\alpha)}$
nodes.statement:
Note that the previous two integral operators commute with the following Gegenbauer-type Sturm-Liouville operator $\mathcal L_c^{(\alpha)},$ defined by
$$
\mathcal L_c^{(\alpha)} (f)(x)= -\frac{1}{\omega_{\alpha}(x)} \frac{d}{dx}\left[ \omega_{\alpha}(x) (1-x^2) f'(x)\right] +c^2 x^2  f(x),\quad \omega_{\alpha}(x)= (1-x^2)^{\alpha}.$$

nodes.name: Classical bounds on the eigenvalues $\chi_n^\alpha(c)$
Bounds on $\chi_n^\alpha(c)$
nodes.statement: n (n+2\alpha+1) \leq \chi_n^{\alpha}(c) \leq n (n+2\alpha+1) +c^2,\quad \forall n\geq 0.
nodes.label: boundschi

nodes.name: GPSWFs $\psi_{n,c}^{(\alpha)}$
nodes.statement: We will denote by$(\psi_{n,c}^{(\alpha)})_{n\geq 0},$ the  set of the eigenfunctions of $\mathcal F_c^{(\alpha)}, \mathcal Q_c^{(\alpha)}$ and $\mathcal L_c^{(\alpha)}.$  They  are called generalized prolate spheroidal wave functions (GPSWFs).

nodes.name: GPSWFs form an orthogonal basis of $L^2(I,\omega_\alpha)$
nodes.statement: It has been shown that $ \{ \psi_{n,c}^{(\alpha)} , n\geq 0 \} $ is an orthogonal basis of $ L^2(I,\omega_{\alpha}), I=[-1,1].$
conclusions: $ \{ \psi_{n,c}^{(\alpha)} , n\geq 0 \} $ is an orthogonal basis of $ L^2(I,\omega_{\alpha}), I=[-1,1].$

nodes.name: Restricted Paley-Wiener space $B_c^{(\alpha)}$
nodes.statement:
We recall that the restricted Paley-Wiener space of weighted $c-$band-limited functions has been defined in \cite{Karoui-Souabni1} by
\begin{equation} B_c^{(\alpha)}=\{ f\in L^2(\mathbb R),\,\,  \mbox{Support } \widehat f\subseteq [-c,c],\, \, \widehat f\in
L^2\big((-c,c), \omega_{- \alpha}(\frac{\cdot}{c})\big)\}.
\end{equation}
Here,  $L^2\big((-c,c), \omega_{- \alpha}(\frac{\cdot}{c})\big)$ is the weighted $L^2(-c,c)-$space with norm given by
$$\| f\|^2_{L^2\big((-c,c), \omega_{- \alpha}(\frac{\cdot}{c})\big)}= \int_{-c}^c |f(t)|^2 \omega_{-\alpha}\left(\frac{t}{c}\right)\, dt.$$
nodes.genus: restricted Paley-Wiener space of weighted $c-$band-limited functions

nodes.name: Restricted Paley-Wiener space $B_c^{(\alpha)}$
nodes.statement: B_c^{(\alpha)}=\{ f\in L^2(\mathbb R),\,\, \mbox{Support } \widehat f\subseteq [-c,c],\, \, \widehat f\in L^2\big((-c,c), \omega_{- \alpha}(\frac{\cdot}{c})\big)\}.
nodes.label: GBc

nodes.name: Super-exponential decay of $\lambda_n^{(\alpha)}(c)$ (Karoui-Souabni)
nodes.statement:
It has been shown in  \cite{Karoui-Souabni1} that the eigenvalues
$\lambda_n^{(\alpha)}(c)$ decay asymptotically at a super-exponential rate that is for $ 0<b<4/e$ there exists $N_b \in \mathbb{N}$ such that :
\begin{equation} \lambda_n^{(\alpha)}(c) < e^{-2n \log(\frac{bn}{c})} \qquad \forall n \geq N_b,
\end{equation}

nodes.name: Decay $\lambda_n < e^{-2n\log(bn/c)}$
nodes.statement: \lambda_n^{(\alpha)}(c) < e^{-2n \log(\frac{bn}{c})} \qquad \forall n \geq N_b,
nodes.label: decaylambda0

nodes.name: Second decay rate of $\lambda_n^{(\alpha)}(c)$ for $0<\alpha<3/2$ (Karoui-Souabni)
nodes.statement:
More precisely, it has been shown in \cite{Karoui-Souabni2}, that if  $c>0$ and $0<\alpha <\frac{3}{2}$, then there exist
$N_{\alpha}(c)\in \mathbb N$ and a constant $C_{\alpha}>0$ such that
\begin{equation} \lambda_n^{(\alpha)}(c) \leq C_{\alpha} \exp\left(-(2n+1)\left[ \log\left(\frac{4n+4\alpha+2}{e c}\right)+ C_{\alpha} \frac{c^2}{2n+1}\right]\right),\quad
\forall\, n\geq N_{\alpha}(c).
\end{equation}
conclusions:
there exist
$N_{\alpha}(c)\in \mathbb N$ and a constant $C_{\alpha}>0$ such that

nodes.name: Decay bound for $\lambda_n$ with $C_\alpha$
nodes.statement: \lambda_n^{(\alpha)}(c) \leq C_{\alpha} \exp\left(-(2n+1)\left[ \log\left(\frac{4n+4\alpha+2}{e c}\right)+ C_{\alpha} \frac{c^2}{2n+1}\right]\right),\quad \forall\, n\geq N_{\alpha}(c).
nodes.label: decay_lambda2

nodes.name: Jacobi expansion coefficients $\beta_k^n$ of the GPSWFs
nodes.statement:
In fact,   since  $\psi^{(\alpha)}_{n,c}\in L^2(I, \omega_{\alpha}),$ then its series expansion
with respect to the Jacobi polynomials basis is given by
\begin{equation} \psi^{(\alpha)}_{n,c}(x) =\sum_{k\geq 0} \beta_k^n \widetilde P^{(\alpha,\alpha)}_k (x),\quad x\in [-1,1].
\end{equation}

nodes.name: Jacobi expansion of $\psi_{n,c}^{(\alpha)}$
nodes.statement: \psi^{(\alpha)}_{n,c}(x) =\sum_{k\geq 0} \beta_k^n \widetilde P^{(\alpha,\alpha)}_k (x),\quad x\in [-1,1].
nodes.label: expansion1

nodes.name: Normalized Jacobi polynomial
Normalized Jacobi polynomial
nodes.statement: \widetilde P^{(\alpha,\alpha)}_{k}(x)= \frac{1}{\sqrt{h_k}}P^{(\alpha,\alpha)}_k(x),\quad h_k=\frac{2^{2\alpha+1}\Gamma^2(k+\alpha+1)}{k!(2k+2\alpha+1)\Gamma(k+2\alpha+1)}.
nodes.label: JacobiP

nodes.name: Three-term eigensystem for the GPSWF Jacobi coefficients
nodes.statement:
The expansion coefficients $\beta_k^n$ as well as the eigenvalues $\chi_n^\alpha(c)$  this system is given by
\begin{eqnarray} \lefteqn{\frac{\sqrt{(k+1)(k+2)(k+2\alpha+1)(k+2\alpha+2)}}{(2k+2\alpha+3)\sqrt{(2k+2\alpha+5)(2k+2\alpha +1)}} c^2 \beta_{k+2}^n
	+ \big( k(k+2\alpha+1)+c^2 \frac{2k(k+2\alpha+1)+2\alpha-1}{(2k+2\alpha+3)(2k+2\alpha-1)} \big)
	\beta_k^n}\nonumber  \\
&&\hspace*{2cm} + \frac{\sqrt{k(k-1)(k+2\alpha)(k+2\alpha-1)}}{(2k+2\alpha-1)\sqrt{(2k+2\alpha+1)(2k+2\alpha-3)}} c^2
\beta_{k-2}^n= \chi_n^{\alpha}(c) \beta_k^n, \quad k\geq 0.
\end{eqnarray}
nodes.statement_short: The coefficients $\beta_k^n$ and $\chi_n^\alpha(c)$ solve a pentadiagonal (step-2) eigensystem.

nodes.name: GPSWF Jacobi eigensystem
nodes.statement: \lefteqn{\frac{\sqrt{(k+1)(k+2)(k+2\alpha+1)(k+2\alpha+2)}}{(2k+2\alpha+3)\sqrt{(2k+2\alpha+5)(2k+2\alpha +1)}} c^2 \beta_{k+2}^n + \big( k(k+2\alpha+1)+c^2 \frac{2k(k+2\alpha+1)+2\alpha-1}{(2k+2\alpha+3)(2k+2\alpha-1)} \big) \beta_k^n}\nonumber \\ &&\hspace*{2cm} + \frac{\sqrt{k(k-1)(k+2\alpha)(k+2\alpha-1)}}{(2k+2\alpha-1)\sqrt{(2k+2\alpha+1)(2k+2\alpha-3)}} c^2 \beta_{k-2}^n= \chi_n^{\alpha}(c) \beta_k^n, \quad k\geq 0.
nodes.label: eigensystem

nodes.name: Jacobi-weighted Sobolev space $H^r_\alpha(I)$
nodes.statement:
We denote, for any $ r \in \mathbb N $, $H^r_{\alpha}(I)$ the Jacobi-weighted Sobolev space by :
$$  H^r_{\alpha}(I) = \{f \in L^2(I,\omega_{\alpha}) : 
orm{f}_{\alpha,r}<\infty \} \quad
\mbox{where} \quad 
orm{f}_{\alpha,r} = \displaystyle{\sum_{k=0}^r 
orm{f^{(k)}}_{\omega}^2} $$
also_stated_at:
Here $ \psi_{n,c}^{(\alpha)}$ are the GPSWFs and $ f \in H^s_{\alpha}(I),$ a weighted Sobolev space defined by:
$$  H^r_{\alpha
}(I) = \{f \in L^2_{I,\omega} : \norm{f}_{\alpha, r}<\infty \} \quad
\mbox{where} \quad \norm{f}^2_{\alpha,r} = \displaystyle{\sum_{k=0}^r \norm{f^{(k)}}_{\omega}^2} $$
equipped with the norm and semi-norm
$$\norm{f}_{\alpha,r} = \displaystyle{\sum_{k=0}^r \norm{f^{(k)}}_{\omega}^2} \quad \mbox{and} \quad |f|_{\alpha,r} = \|f^{(k)}\|_{\omega_{\alpha}} $$

nodes.name: Weighted Sobolev space $H^r_\alpha$ for real $r$ (interpolation)
nodes.statement: For any real r, we define the weighted Sobolev space $H^r_{\alpha}$ by interpolation  $ H^r_{\alpha} = \Big[H^{[r]}_{\alpha},H^{[r]+1}_{\alpha}\Big]$ as it is done in \cite{Bergh-Lofstrom} and \cite{Bernardi-Maday}

nodes.name: $\mathcal{C}_{\infty}(I)$
nodes.statement: We denote by $ \mathcal{C}_{\infty}(I) $ the set of infinitely differentiable functions defined on $ I $.

nodes.name: Sobolev space $H_0^s(I)$
nodes.statement: Let $H_0^s(I) $ be the completion of $ \mathcal{C}_{\infty}(I) $ in $H^s(I)$.

nodes.name: $H_0^s(I)$ for real $s$ by interpolation
nodes.statement: For $s\geq 0$, we define $H_0^s(I) $by interpolation as in \cite{Bergh-Lofstrom} and \cite{Bernardi-Maday}.

nodes.name: Proof of Theorem 2/3 (eigenvalue decay)
nodes.statement_short: Courant-Fischer min-max with the span of the first $n$ Jacobi polynomials, bounding $\|\mathcal F \widetilde P_k\|$ via Bessel and Gamma inequalities. The tail sum is compared with an integral.

nodes.name: Courant-Fischer-Weyl Min-Max variational principle
nodes.statement:
We first recall the Courant-Fischer-Weyl Min-Max variational principle concerning the eigenvalues
of a  compact self-adjoint operator $T$ on a Hilbert space $\mathcal G,$ with positive eigenvalues arranged in the decreasing order $\lambda_0\geq \lambda_1\geq \cdots\geq \lambda_n\geq \cdots ,$ then we have
$$\lambda_n = \min_{f\in S_n}\,\,\,  \max_{f\in S_n^{\perp},\|f\|_{\mathcal G}=1} < Tf, f>_{\mathcal G},$$
where $S_n$ is a subspace of $\mathcal G$ of dimension $n.$
assumptions: a  compact self-adjoint operator $T$ on a Hilbert space $\mathcal G,$ with positive eigenvalues arranged in the decreasing order $\lambda_0\geq \lambda_1\geq \cdots\geq \lambda_n\geq \cdots ,$
conclusions: $$\lambda_n = \min_{f\in S_n}\,\,\,  \max_{f\in S_n^{\perp},\|f\|_{\mathcal G}=1} < Tf, f>_{\mathcal G},$$

nodes.name: Norm of $\mathcal F_c^{(\alpha)} P_k^{(\alpha,\alpha)}$ (NIST)
nodes.statement: \| \mathcal F_c^{(\alpha)} P^{(\alpha,\alpha)}_k\|_{L^2(I,\omega_{\alpha})} = \parallel \sqrt{\pi} \left(\frac{2}{cx}\right) ^{\alpha+1/2} \frac{\Gamma(k+\alpha+1)}{\Gamma(k+1)}J_{k+\alpha+1/2}(cx) \parallel_{L^2(I,\omega_{\alpha})}.
nodes.label: Eq3.2

nodes.name: Weighted norm of $x^k$
nodes.statement: \parallel x^k \parallel_{L^2(I,\omega_{\alpha})}^2=\beta(k+1/2,\alpha+1)\leq \sqrt{\frac{\pi}{e}}\frac{\Gamma(\alpha+1)}{k^{\alpha+1}}.

nodes.name: Bessel function bound
nodes.statement: |J_{\alpha}(x)|\leq \frac{|x|^{\alpha}}{2^{\alpha}\Gamma(\alpha+1)}\;\;\;\;\;\;\;\;\forall\alpha>-1/2, \;\; \forall x \in \mathbb{R},

nodes.name: First bound on $\|\mathcal F_c^{(\alpha)}\widetilde P_k\|$
nodes.statement: \| \mathcal F_c^{(\alpha)} \widetilde P^{(\alpha,\alpha)}_k\|_{L^2(I,\omega_{\alpha})} &\leq & \frac{\sqrt{\pi}\Gamma(k+\alpha+1)}{\sqrt{h_k}\Gamma(k+1)\Gamma(k+\alpha+3/2)}\left(\frac{c}{2}\right) ^{k} \parallel x^k \parallel_{L^2(I,\omega_{\alpha})}. \nonumber\\ &\leq & \frac{\sqrt{\pi}\Gamma(k+\alpha+1)}{\sqrt{h_k}\Gamma(k+1)\Gamma(k+\alpha+3/2)}\left(\frac{c}{2}\right) ^{k}\left(\frac{\pi}{e}\right)^{1/4}\frac{\sqrt{\Gamma(\alpha+1)}}{k^{\frac{\alpha+1}{2}}}

nodes.name: Batir's inequalities for the Gamma function
nodes.statement: \sqrt{2e}\left(\frac{x+1/2}{e}\right)^{x+1/2}\leq\Gamma(x+1)\leq \sqrt{2\pi}\left(\frac{x+1/2}{e}\right)^{x+1/2}\;,\;\;\; x>0.

nodes.name: Second bound on $\|\mathcal F_c^{(\alpha)}\widetilde P_k\|$
nodes.statement: \| \mathcal F_c^{(\alpha)} \widetilde P^{(\alpha,\alpha)}_k\|_{L^2(I,\omega_{\alpha})} &\leq & \frac{\sqrt{\pi}\sqrt{(k+\alpha+\frac{1}{2})\Gamma(k+2\alpha+1)}}{2^{\alpha+\frac{1}{2}}\sqrt{\Gamma(k+1)}\Gamma(k+\alpha+\frac{3}{2})}\left(\frac{c}{2}\right) ^{k}\left(\frac{\pi}{e}\right)^{\frac{1}{4}}\frac{\sqrt{\Gamma(\alpha+1)}}{k^{\frac{\alpha+1}{2}}}\nonumber\\ &=&\frac{\pi \sqrt{\Gamma(\alpha+1)}\big(k+2\alpha+\frac{1}{2}\Big)^{\frac{k}{2}+\alpha+\frac{1}{4 }}}{\sqrt{ec}2^{\alpha}k^{\frac{\alpha+1}{2}}\left(k+\frac{1}{2}\right)^{\frac{k}{2}+\frac{1}{4}}\left(k+\alpha+1\right)^{k+\alpha+\frac{1}{2}}} \left(\frac{ce}{2}\right) ^{k+\frac{1}{2 }}\nonumber\\ &=&\frac{\pi \sqrt{\Gamma(\alpha+1)}}{\sqrt{ec}2^{\alpha}k^{\frac{\alpha+1}{2}}}\left(1+\frac{\alpha-\frac{1}{2}}{k+\alpha+1}\right)^{\frac{k}{2}+\alpha+\frac{1}{4}} \left(\frac{ce}{2k+1}\right) ^{k+\frac{1}{2}}.

nodes.name: Bound (24) on $\|\mathcal F_c^{(\alpha)}\widetilde P_k\|$
nodes.statement: \| \mathcal F_c^{(\alpha)} \widetilde P^{(\alpha,\alpha)}_k\|_{L^2(I,\omega_{\alpha})} &\leq &\frac{\pi \sqrt{\Gamma(\alpha+1)}}{\sqrt{c}k^{\frac{\alpha+1}{2}}} \left(\frac{ce}{2k+1}\right) ^{k+\frac{1}{2}}.

nodes.name: Bound on $<\mathcal F^*\mathcal F f,f>$
nodes.statement: |< \mathcal F_c^{\alpha^*}\mathcal F_c^{(\alpha)} f,f>_{L^2(I,\omega_{\alpha})}|&=&|< \mathcal F_c^{(\alpha)} f,\mathcal F_c^{(\alpha)}f>_{L^2(I,\omega_{\alpha})}| \leq \sum_{k\geq n} |a_k|^2 \| \mathcal F_c^{(\alpha)} \widetilde P^{(\alpha,\alpha)}_k\|^2_{L^2(I,\omega_{\alpha})}\\ &\leq&\left(\frac{2^\frac{1}{4}\pi \sqrt{\Gamma(\alpha+1)}}{\sqrt{ec}} \sum_{k\geq n} \left(\frac{ec}{2k+1}\right)^{k+1/2}\frac{1}{k^{\frac{\alpha+1}{2}}}\right)^2
nodes.label: Eq3.3

nodes.name: Sum-integral comparison
nodes.statement: \sum_{k\geq n} \left(\frac{ec}{2k+1}\right)^{k+1/2}\frac{1}{k^{\frac{\alpha+1}{2}}} \leq \int_{n-1}^{\infty}\frac{ e^{-(x+1/2) \log(\frac{2x+1}{ec})}}{x^{\frac{\alpha+1}{2}}}\, dx\leq \int_{n-1}^{\infty}\frac{ e^{-(x+1/2)\log(\frac{2n-1}{ec})}}{(n-1)^{\frac{\alpha+1}{2}}}\, dx.
nodes.label: Eq3.4

nodes.name: Max over $S_n^\perp$ bound
nodes.statement: \max_{f\in S_n^{\perp},\, \|f\|_{L^2(I,\omega_{\alpha})=1}} < \mathcal F_c^{(\alpha)} f, \mathcal F_c^{(\alpha)} f>^{1/2}_{L^2(I,\omega_{\alpha})}&\leq &\frac{2^\frac{1}{4}\pi \sqrt{\Gamma(\alpha+1)}}{\sqrt{ec}} \frac{1}{\log(\frac{2n-1}{ec})} \left(\frac{ec}{2n-1}\right)^{n-1/2}\frac{1}{(n-1)^{\frac{\alpha+1}{2}}}\nonumber\\ &\leq&\pi \sqrt{\Gamma(\alpha+1)} \left(\frac{2}{ec}\right)^{\frac{\alpha+2}{2}} \frac{1}{\log(\frac{2n-1}{ec})} \left(\frac{ec}{2n-1}\right)^{n+\frac{\alpha}{2}}
nodes.label: Eq3.5

nodes.name: Recall min-max principle
nodes.statement:
We first recall the Courant-Fischer-Weyl Min-Max variational principle concerning the eigenvalues
of a  compact self-adjoint operator $T$ on a Hilbert space $\mathcal G,$ with positive eigenvalues arranged in the decreasing order $\lambda_0\geq \lambda_1\geq \cdots\geq \lambda_n\geq \cdots ,$ then we have
$$\lambda_n = \min_{f\in S_n}\,\,\,  \max_{f\in S_n^{\perp},\|f\|_{\mathcal G}=1} < Tf, f>_{\mathcal G},$$
where $S_n$ is a subspace of $\mathcal G$ of dimension $n.$ In our case, we have $T=\mathcal F_c^{\alpha^*}\mathcal F_c^{(\alpha)},$ $\mathcal G= L^2(I,\omega_{\alpha}).$
nodes.statement_short: Recall Courant-Fischer-Weyl min-max and specialise $T=\mathcal F^*\mathcal F$.

nodes.name: Choose subspace and test function
nodes.statement:
We consider the special case of  $$S_n=\mbox{Span}\left\{\widetilde P^{(\alpha,\alpha)}_0, \widetilde P^{(\alpha,\alpha)}_1,\ldots,\widetilde P^{(\alpha,\alpha)}_{n-1}\right\}$$ and
$$f=\displaystyle\sum_{k\geq n} a_k \widetilde P^{(\alpha,\alpha)}_k \in S_n^{\perp},\qquad
\parallel f\parallel_{L^2_{(I,\omega_\alpha)}}=\displaystyle\sum_{k\geq n}|a_k|^2=1.$$
Here the $ \widetilde P^{(\alpha,\alpha)}_{k} $ are the normalized Jacobi polynomials given by \eqref{JacobiP}.
nodes.statement_short: Take $S_n$ spanned by the first $n$ normalized Jacobi polynomials and $f\in S_n^\perp$.

nodes.name: NIST formulas
nodes.statement:
From [\cite{NIST} page 456], we have
\begin{equation} \| \mathcal F_c^{(\alpha)} P^{(\alpha,\alpha)}_k\|_{L^2(I,\omega_{\alpha})} = \parallel \sqrt{\pi} \left(\frac{2}{cx}\right) ^{\alpha+1/2} \frac{\Gamma(k+\alpha+1)}{\Gamma(k+1)}J_{k+\alpha+1/2}(cx)
\parallel_{L^2(I,\omega_{\alpha})}.
\end{equation}
and
\begin{equation} \parallel  x^k
\parallel_{L^2(I,\omega_{\alpha})}^2=\beta(k+1/2,\alpha+1)\leq \sqrt{\frac{\pi}{e}}\frac{\Gamma(\alpha+1)}{k^{\alpha+1}}.
\end{equation}
nodes.statement_short: Quote the norm of $\mathcal F P_k$ and the weighted norm of $x^k$.

nodes.name: Apply Bessel bound
nodes.statement_short: Bound $\|\mathcal F\widetilde P_k\|$ via the Bessel bound.

nodes.name: Apply Gamma inequalities
nodes.statement_short: Use Batir's Gamma inequalities to simplify the bound.

nodes.name: Monotonicity of $g_a$
nodes.statement_short: Monotonicity of $g_a$ yields bound (24).

nodes.name: Bound the quadratic form
nodes.statement_short: Hölder and Minkowski bound $<\mathcal F^*\mathcal F f,f>$ by a series.

nodes.name: Compare sum with integral
nodes.statement_short: Compare the tail series with an integral.

nodes.name: Combine bounds
nodes.statement_short: Combine to bound the max over $S_n^\perp$.

nodes.name: Conclude by min-max
nodes.statement: To conclude the proof of the theorem, it suffices to use the Courant-Fischer-Weyl Min-Max variational principle.$\qquad \Box $
nodes.statement_short: Apply min-max to conclude.

nodes.name: Improvement over earlier decay rates
nodes.statement: The decay rate given by the last proposition improve the two results mentioned above \eqref{decaylambda0} and \eqref{decay_lambda2}. Indeed, we have a more precise result furthermore the proof given in \cite{Karoui-Souabni2} contains two serious drawbacks. It is only valid in the particular case $0 < \alpha < 3/2 $ and clearly more sophisticated than the previous one.
nodes.statement_short: The new bound improves the decay rates of Karoui-Souabni and holds for all $\alpha\ge 0$ with a simpler proof.

nodes.name: GPSWF Sturm-Liouville ODE
nodes.statement: \omega_{\alpha}(x)\mathcal L_c^{(\alpha)} \psi(x)+w_{\alpha}(x)\chi_{n,\alpha}\psi(x)= ( w_{\alpha}(x)\psi'(x)(1-x^2))'+ w_{\alpha}(x)(\chi_{n}^{\alpha}-c^2 x^2)\psi(x)=0,\quad x\in [-1,1].
nodes.label: eq2_diff

nodes.name: Incomplete elliptic integral $S(x)$ and $q$
Liouville transform $S(x)$
nodes.statement: S(x)=\int_x^1 \sqrt{\frac{1-qt^2}{1-t^2}}\, dt,\qquad q=\frac{c^2}{\chi_n^\alpha(c)}<1.
nodes.label: Liouvile_transform1

nodes.name: Liouville transform $\psi=\phi_\alpha V(S)$
Liouville form of $\psi$
nodes.statement: \psi(x)=\phi_{\alpha}(x)V(S(x)),\qquad \phi_{\alpha}(x)=(1-x^2)^{(-1-2\alpha)/4} (1-qx^2)^{-1/4}.
nodes.label: Liouvile_transform2

nodes.name: ODE for $V$ after the Liouville transform
nodes.statement_short: $V$ satisfies $V''+(\chi+\theta_\alpha)V=0$ with explicit potential $\theta_\alpha$.
conclusions: $V(\cdot)$ satisfies the following second order differential equation

nodes.name: Normal-form ODE for $V$
nodes.statement: V''(s)+\left(\chi_{n,\alpha}+\theta_{\alpha}(s)\right)V(s)=0,\quad s\in [0, S(0)]

nodes.name: $Q_\alpha$
nodes.statement:
Define $ Q_{\alpha}(x)=w_{\alpha}(x)^2(1-x^2)(1-qx^2),$ then we have
${\displaystyle  \frac{\phi_{\alpha}'(x)}{\phi_{\alpha}(x)}=-1/4 \frac{Q_{\alpha}'(x)}{Q_{\alpha}(x)}. }$

nodes.name: Formula for $\theta_\alpha$ via $Q_\alpha$
Expression of $\theta_\alpha(S(x))$
nodes.statement: \theta_{\alpha}(S(x))=\frac{1}{16(1-qx^2)}\Big[\Big(\frac{Q_{\alpha}'(x)}{Q_{\alpha}(x)}\Big)^2(1-x^2)-4\frac{d}{dx}\Big((1-x^2)\frac{Q_{\alpha}'(x)}{Q_{\alpha}(x)}\Big)-4(1-x^2)\frac{Q_{\alpha}'(x)}{Q_{\alpha}(x)} \frac{w_{\alpha}'(x)}{w_{\alpha}(x)}\Big].

nodes.name: Derivation of $\theta_\alpha=\theta_0+\dots$
nodes.statement:
Since $ Q_{\alpha}(x)=w_{\alpha}^2(x)Q_0(x),$ then we have
${\displaystyle  \frac{Q_{\alpha}'(x)}{Q_{\alpha}(x)}=2\frac{w_{\alpha}'(x)}{w_{\alpha}(x)}+\frac{Q_0'(x)}{Q_0(x)}} $ and ${\displaystyle \frac{w_{\alpha}'(x)}{w_{\alpha}(x)}=-\frac{2\alpha x}{1-x^2}.} $
nodes.statement_short: Split $Q_\alpha'/Q_\alpha$ into weight and $Q_0$ parts.

nodes.name: Perturbation formula $\theta_\alpha=\theta_0+\dots$
nodes.statement_short: $\theta_\alpha(S(x))=\theta_0(S(x))+\frac{\alpha(1+\alpha)}{1-qx^2}-\frac{\alpha^2}{(1-qx^2)(1-x^2)}$.

nodes.name: $\theta_\alpha$ in terms of $\theta_0$
nodes.statement: \theta_{\alpha}(S(x)) &=&\theta_0(S(x))+\frac{-1}{4(1-qx^2)}\Big[ \big(\frac{w_{\alpha}'(x)}{w_{\alpha}(x)}\big)^2 (1-x^2)+2\frac{d}{dx}[(1-x^2)\frac{w_{\alpha}'(x)}{w_{\alpha}(x)}] \Big] \nonumber \\ &=&\theta_0(S(x))+ \frac{1}{(1-x^2)(1-qx^2)}\Big( -\alpha^2 x^2 + \alpha (1-x^2) \Big) \nonumber \\ &=&\theta_0(S(x))+ \frac{\alpha(1+\alpha)}{(1-qx^2)}-\frac{\alpha^2}{(1-q x^2)(1-x^2)}.

nodes.name: Monotonicity of $\theta_\alpha(S(x))$
nodes.statement: For any $0\leq \alpha\leq \frac{1}{4}$ and $0<q=c^2/\chi_n^{\alpha}(c) <\frac{3}{17}$, we have $\theta_{\alpha}(S(x))$ is increasing on $ [0.1]$.\\

nodes.name: Proof of Lemma 1
nodes.statement: We use the notation $u=1-x^2$ and with straightforward computations, we have \begin{eqnarray*} (\theta_{\alpha}(S(x)))'&=&(\theta_{0}(S(x)))'+\frac{2x}{(1-qx^2)^2(1-x^2)^2}\left[q\alpha(\alpha+1)(1-x^2)^2 -q\alpha^2(1-x^2)-\alpha^2(1-qx^2)\right] \\ &=& \frac{2xH(u)}{4u^2(1-q+qu)^4} \end{eqnarray*} where \begin{eqnarray*} H(u) &=& G(u)+4(1-q+qu^2)^2[q(\alpha^2+\alpha)u^2-\alpha^2(1-q+2qu)]\\ &\geq&(1-q+qu^2)^2[G(u)+4[q(\alpha^2+\alpha)u^2-\alpha^2(1-q+2qu)]] \end{eqnarray*} with $G(u)\geq\frac{(1-q)^2}{4}(4-4q+u(17q-3))\geq0,\;\;\forall q>0,\;\;\alpha>0$ then \begin{eqnarray*} H(u) &\geq&(1-q+qu^2)^2\left[ \frac{(1-q)^2}{4}(4-4q+u(17q-3))+4[-q\frac{\alpha^3}{\alpha+1}-(1-q)\alpha^2]\right] \\ &\geq& (1-q+qu^2)^2\left[(1-q)^3-4\alpha^2(1-q\frac{1}{\alpha+1})+\frac{(1-q)^2}{4}(17q-3)u\right]. \end{eqnarray*} Then if $0\leq q\leq\frac{3}{17}$ and $\alpha\leq \frac{1}{4}$ we have \begin{eqnarray*} H(u) &\geq& (1-q+qu^2)^2 \left[(1-q)^3-4\alpha^2(1-q\frac{1}{\alpha+1})+\frac{(1-q)^2}{4}(17q-3)\right]\nonumber\\ &\geq &(1-q+qu^2)^2\left[\frac{(1-q)^2}{4}(1+13q)-4\alpha^2\right]\geq0 \end{eqnarray*} $\qquad \Box $
nodes.statement_short: Differentiate $\theta_\alpha(S(x))$ in $u=1-x^2$ and show the numerator $H(u)\ge 0$ for $q\le 3/17$, $\alpha\le 1/4$.

nodes.name: Local estimate of the GPSWFs
nodes.statement: For any $0\leq \alpha\leq \frac{1}{4}$ and for any integer $n\in \mathbb N,$ with $0<q=\frac{c^2}{\chi_n^\alpha(c)} <\frac{3}{17}$, we have \begin{equation} \displaystyle{\sup_{x\in[0,1]}}\sqrt{(1-x^2)(1-qx^2)}\omega_{\alpha}(x)|\psi_{n,c}^{(\alpha)}(x)|^2\leq|\psi_{n,c}^{(\alpha)}(0)|^2+ \frac{|{\psi_{n,c}^{(\alpha)}}'(0)|^2}{\chi_n^{\alpha}(c)}= A^2 \leq 2 \alpha + 1 \; \end{equation}
nodes.statement_short: For $0\le\alpha\le 1/4$ and $q<3/17$, the weighted sup of $|\psi_{n,c}^{(\alpha)}|^2$ on $[0,1]$ is at most $2\alpha+1$.

nodes.name: Local estimate of $\psi_{n,c}^{(\alpha)}$
nodes.statement: \displaystyle{\sup_{x\in[0,1]}}\sqrt{(1-x^2)(1-qx^2)}\omega_{\alpha}(x)|\psi_{n,c}^{(\alpha)}(x)|^2\leq|\psi_{n,c}^{(\alpha)}(0)|^2+ \frac{|{\psi_{n,c}^{(\alpha)}}'(0)|^2}{\chi_n^{\alpha}(c)}= A^2 \leq 2 \alpha + 1 \;
nodes.label: estimation

nodes.name: Proof of Lemma 2
nodes.statement: For $0\leq \alpha\leq \frac{1}{4}$ and $0<q<\frac{3}{17}$ ,we have $ \theta_{\alpha} \circ S $ is increasing. Since $S$ is decreasing then $ \theta $ is also decreasing. We define $K(s)= |V(s)|^2 + \frac{1}{\chi_n^{\alpha}(c)+\theta(s)}|V'(s)|^2 $ By the fact that $K(s)$ and $ \frac{1}{\chi_n^{\alpha}(c)+\theta(s)} $ has the same monotonicity and $\theta$ is decreasing , we conclude that $ K $ is increasing. Then $$ |V(S(x))|^2 \leq |K(S(x)) | \leq |K(S(0)) | $$ We remark easily that $ V(S(0)) = \psi_{n,c}^{(\alpha)}(0) $ and $ V'(S(0)) ={ \psi_{n,c}^{(\alpha)}}'(0) $ then we conclude for the first inequality of \eqref{estimation}. The second inequality is given later on remark \ref{rq}
nodes.statement_short: Energy functional $K(s)=|V|^2+|V'|^2/(\chi+\theta)$ is monotone since $\theta$ is decreasing; evaluate at $s=S(0)$.

nodes.name: Monotonicity of $\theta$
nodes.statement: For $0\leq  \alpha\leq \frac{1}{4}$ and $0<q<\frac{3}{17}$ ,we have $ \theta_{\alpha} \circ S $ is increasing. Since $S$ is decreasing then $ \theta $ is also decreasing.
nodes.statement_short: By Lemma 1, $\theta$ is decreasing.

nodes.name: Energy functional $K$
nodes.statement:
We define $K(s)= |V(s)|^2 + \frac{1}{\chi_n^{\alpha}(c)+\theta(s)}|V'(s)|^2 $
	By the fact that $K(s)$ and $ \frac{1}{\chi_n^{\alpha}(c)+\theta(s)} $ has the same monotonicity and  $\theta$ is decreasing , we conclude that $ K $ is increasing.
nodes.statement_short: Define $K(s)$ and show it is increasing.

nodes.name: Bound by $K(S(0))$
nodes.statement: Then $$ |V(S(x))|^2 \leq |K(S(x)) | \leq |K(S(0)) | $$
nodes.statement_short: Bound $|V(S(x))|^2$ by $K(S(0))$.

nodes.name: Evaluate at $x=0$
nodes.statement: We remark easily that $ V(S(0)) = \psi_{n,c}^{(\alpha)}(0) $ and $ V'(S(0)) ={ \psi_{n,c}^{(\alpha)}}'(0) $ then we conclude for the first inequality of \eqref{estimation}.
nodes.statement_short: Identify $K(S(0))$ with $A^2$: first inequality.

nodes.name: Forward pointer to Remark
nodes.statement: The second inequality is given later on remark \ref{rq}
nodes.statement_short: Second inequality deferred to Remark 2.

nodes.name: Lower and upper bounds for $\chi_n^\alpha(c)$
nodes.statement: For c and n such that $0\leq \alpha\leq \frac{1}{4}$ and $0<q<\frac{3}{17}$, we have : \begin{equation} n(n+2\alpha+1)+C_\alpha c^2 \leq \chi_n^{\alpha}(c) \leq n(n+2\alpha+1)+c^2 \end{equation} Where $$ C_{\alpha} = 2(2\alpha+1)^2+1 - 2(2\alpha+1)\sqrt{1+(2\alpha+1)^2}.$$
nodes.statement_short: For $0\le\alpha\le1/4$, $q<3/17$: $n(n+2\alpha+1)+C_\alpha c^2\le\chi_n^\alpha(c)\le n(n+2\alpha+1)+c^2$.

nodes.name: Two-sided bound on $\chi_n^\alpha(c)$
nodes.statement: n(n+2\alpha+1)+C_\alpha c^2 \leq \chi_n^{\alpha}(c) \leq n(n+2\alpha+1)+c^2
nodes.label: chi_n

nodes.name: Proof of Proposition 1
nodes.statement: By differentiating with respect to $c$ the differential equation satisfied by GPSWFs , one gets $$ (1-x^2) \partial_c {{\psi_{n,c}^{(\alpha)}}'}'(x) - 2(\alpha+1)x \partial_c {\psi_{n,c}^{(\alpha)}}'(x) + (\chi_n^{\alpha}(c)-c^2x^2) \partial_c \psi_{n,c}^{(\alpha)}(x) + \Big( \partial_c \chi_n^{\alpha}(c)-2cx^2 \Big) \psi_{n,c}^{(\alpha)}(x) = 0 $$ Hence, we have $$ \Big(\mathcal{L}^{(\alpha)}_c + \chi_n^{\alpha}(c)Id\Big).\partial_c \psi_{n,c}^{(\alpha)} + \Big( \partial_c \chi_n^{\alpha}(c)-2cx^2 \Big) \psi_{n,c}^{(\alpha)}(x) = 0 $$ It's well known that $\mathcal{L}^{(\alpha)}_c $ is a self-adjoint operator and have $ \psi_{n,c}^{(\alpha)}$ as eigenfunctions . Hence, we have $$ < \Big(\mathcal{L}^{(\alpha)}_c + \chi_n^{\alpha}(c)Id\Big).\partial_c \psi_{n,c}^{(\alpha)}; \psi_{n,c}^{(\alpha)}>_{\omega_{\alpha}} = 0 $$ It follows that $$ \int_{-1}^{1} \Big( \partial_c \chi_n^{\alpha}(c)-2cx^2 \Big) {\psi_{n,c}^{(\alpha)}} ^{2}(x) dx = 0. $$ From the fact that $ \norm{\psi_{n,c}^{(\alpha)}}_{L^2(I,\omega_\alpha)} = 1 $, one gets \begin{equation} \partial_c \chi_n^{\alpha}(c) = 2c \int_{-1}^{1} x^2 {\psi_{n,c}^{(\alpha)}}^2(x) \omega_{\alpha}(x) dx \end{equation} As it is done in \cite{Bonami-Karoui1}, we denote by $ A= \Bigg[\psi_{n,c}^{(\alpha)}(0) + \frac{{\psi_{n,c}^{(\alpha)}}'(0)}{\chi_n^{\alpha}(c)} \Bigg]^{1/2} $ and consider the auxiliary function $$ K_n(t) = - (1-t^2)^{2\alpha+1} {\psi_{n,c}^{(\alpha)}}^2 - \frac{(1-t^2)^{2\alpha+2}}{\chi_n^{\alpha}(c)(1-qt^2)}({\psi_{n,c}^{(\alpha)}}')^2 $$ Straightforward computations give us $$ K'_n(t) = 2(2\alpha+1)t(1-t^2)^{2\alpha} {\psi_{n,c}^{(\alpha)}}^2(t) - {H(t) {\psi_{n,c}^{(\alpha)}}'(t)}^2 $$ with $ H(t) \geq 0 $ for $t\in[0,1]$. Hence $$ K'_n(t) \leq 2(2\alpha+1)t\omega_{\alpha}^2(t) {\psi_{n,c}^{(\alpha)}}^2(t) \leq 2(2\alpha+1)t\omega_{\alpha}(t) {\psi_{n,c}^{(\alpha)}}^2(t). $$ So one has the inequality \begin{equation} K_n(1) - K_n(0) = A^2 \leq 2(2\alpha+1) \int_{0}^{1} t{|\psi_{n,c}^{(\alpha)}(t) |}^2 \omega_{\alpha}(t) dt \leq (2\alpha+1) \Bigg[\int_{-1}^{1}t^2 |\psi_{n,c}^{(\alpha)}(t) |^2 \omega_{\alpha}(t) dt \Bigg] ^{1/2}. \end{equation} That is \begin{equation} A^2 \leq (2\alpha+1) B^{1/2}. \end{equation} Remark that \eqref{estimation} implies that \begin{equation} 1-B \leq 2 A^2 \end{equation} By combining \eqref{11} and \eqref{12} we conclude that $B^{1/2} $ is bounded below by the largest solution of the equation $ X^2 + 2(2\alpha+1) X -1 = 0 $
nodes.statement_short: Differentiate the ODE in $c$ to get $\partial_c\chi_n=2c\int x^2\psi^2\omega$, then bound $B=\int x^2\psi^2\omega$ below with an auxiliary function $K_n$ and the local estimate.

nodes.name: Differentiate the ODE in $c$
nodes.statement:
By differentiating with respect to $c$ the differential equation satisfied by GPSWFs , one gets
	$$ (1-x^2) \partial_c {{\psi_{n,c}^{(\alpha)}}'}'(x) - 2(\alpha+1)x \partial_c {\psi_{n,c}^{(\alpha)}}'(x)
	+ (\chi_n^{\alpha}(c)-c^2x^2) \partial_c \psi_{n,c}^{(\alpha)}(x) + \Big( \partial_c \chi_n^{\alpha}(c)-2cx^2 \Big) \psi_{n,c}^{(\alpha)}(x) = 0 $$
	Hence, we have
	$$ \Big(\mathcal{L}^{(\alpha)}_c + \chi_n^{\alpha}(c)Id\Big).\partial_c \psi_{n,c}^{(\alpha)} + \Big( \partial_c \chi_n^{\alpha}(c)-2cx^2 \Big) \psi_{n,c}^{(\alpha)}(x) = 0 $$
nodes.statement_short: Differentiate the GPSWF ODE with respect to $c$.

nodes.name: Self-adjointness gives $\partial_c\chi_n$
nodes.statement:
It's well known that $\mathcal{L}^{(\alpha)}_c $ is a self-adjoint operator and have $ \psi_{n,c}^{(\alpha)}$ as eigenfunctions . Hence, we have
	$$ < \Big(\mathcal{L}^{(\alpha)}_c + \chi_n^{\alpha}(c)Id\Big).\partial_c \psi_{n,c}^{(\alpha)}; \psi_{n,c}^{(\alpha)}>_{\omega_{\alpha}} = 0 $$
It follows that
	$$ \int_{-1}^{1} \Big( \partial_c \chi_n^{\alpha}(c)-2cx^2 \Big) {\psi_{n,c}^{(\alpha)}} ^{2}(x) dx = 0. $$
	From the fact that $ \norm{\psi_{n,c}^{(\alpha)}}_{L^2(I,\omega_\alpha)} = 1 $, one gets
	\begin{equation} \partial_c \chi_n^{\alpha}(c) = 2c \int_{-1}^{1} x^2 {\psi_{n,c}^{(\alpha)}}^2(x) \omega_{\alpha}(x) dx
	\end{equation}
nodes.statement_short: Self-adjointness and normalization give $\partial_c\chi_n=2c\int x^2\psi^2\omega$.

nodes.name: Auxiliary function $K_n$
nodes.statement:
As it is done in \cite{Bonami-Karoui1}, we denote by $ A= \Bigg[\psi_{n,c}^{(\alpha)}(0) + \frac{{\psi_{n,c}^{(\alpha)}}'(0)}{\chi_n^{\alpha}(c)} \Bigg]^{1/2} $ and consider the auxiliary function $$ K_n(t) = - (1-t^2)^{2\alpha+1} {\psi_{n,c}^{(\alpha)}}^2 - \frac{(1-t^2)^{2\alpha+2}}{\chi_n^{\alpha}(c)(1-qt^2)}({\psi_{n,c}^{(\alpha)}}')^2 $$
	Straightforward computations give us $$ K'_n(t) = 2(2\alpha+1)t(1-t^2)^{2\alpha} {\psi_{n,c}^{(\alpha)}}^2(t) - {H(t) {\psi_{n,c}^{(\alpha)}}'(t)}^2 $$ with $ H(t) \geq 0 $  for $t\in[0,1]$. Hence
	$$ K'_n(t)  \leq 2(2\alpha+1)t\omega_{\alpha}^2(t) {\psi_{n,c}^{(\alpha)}}^2(t) \leq 2(2\alpha+1)t\omega_{\alpha}(t) {\psi_{n,c}^{(\alpha)}}^2(t).  $$
nodes.statement_short: Introduce $A$ and auxiliary function $K_n$ and bound $K_n'$.

nodes.name: Integrate $K_n'$
nodes.statement_short: Integrate to get $A^2\le(2\alpha+1)B^{1/2}$.

nodes.statement_short: Local estimate gives $1-B\le 2A^2$.

nodes.name: Combine
nodes.statement:
By combining \eqref{11} and \eqref{12} we conclude that $B^{1/2} $ is bounded below by the largest solution of the equation
	$ X^2 + 2(2\alpha+1) X -1 = 0 $
nodes.statement_short: Combine to bound $B^{1/2}$ below by the root of a quadratic.

nodes.name: Second inequality of the local estimate
nodes.statement: By using \eqref{11} and since $B\leq1$, one concludes that the constant $A,$ given in \eqref{estimation} satisfies $A^2\leq 2\alpha+1.$
nodes.statement_short: From (11) and $B\le 1$, $A^2\le 2\alpha+1$.

nodes.name: Approximation of a Brownian motion function
nodes.statement:
{\bf Example 2:} In this example, for a positive real number $s$, we consider the Brownian motion function  
$$ B_s(x) = \sum_{k=1}^{\infty} \frac{X_k}{k^s} \cos(k \pi x) \quad x\in I=[-1,1] $$
Here $X_k$ is a sequence of independent standard Gaussian random variable. It is well known that $B_s\in H^{s'-1/2}(I),$ for any
$s'< s-\frac{1}{2}.$ Here, $H^s(I)$ is the  Sobolev space over $I,$ with smoothness exponent $s.$ For the special values of 
$s=1.5$ and  $ c= 5\pi $, and the two values of $N=46$ and $N=90,$ we have computed $S_N(B_s),$ the truncated series expansion to the order $N,$ of $B_s$ in the GPSWFs basis. We have found that 
$$\| B_s - S_{46}(B_s)\|_{\infty} \approx 01 E-01,\qquad \| B_s - S_{90}(B_s)\|_{\infty} \approx 05 E-02.$$
Moreover, the graphs of $B_{s}$ and  of its approximation  $S_{90} B_{s}$ are given by the figure \ref{brownian}.
nodes.statement_short: GPSWF truncations $S_{46}$, $S_{90}$ of a random Brownian-type series $B_s$ give sup errors $\approx 10^{-1}$, $5\cdot10^{-2}$.

nodes.statement:
{\bf Example 2:}To illustrate approximation by GPSWFs we have considered the Weierstrass-Mondelbrot function given by :

$$ M_{s,\lambda}(x) = \sum_{k=0}^{\infty} \frac{\sin(\lambda^k x)}{\lambda^{k(2-s)}} $$
For $\lambda > 1 $ and $s<1$, $M_{s,\lambda} \in H^s_{\alpha}(I)$
In this example we have considered the values of $\alpha = 0.5$, $c=5\pi$ and $N=95$ then we have computed the projection, over $Span(\psi_{0,c}^{(\alpha)}, \cdots , \psi_{N,c}^{(\alpha)})$, $S_N(M_{s,\lambda}(x)) $. For this purpose, we have computed the different expansion coefficients $ \displaystyle{ C_n(M_{s,\lambda}(x)) = \int_{-1}^{1}M_{s,\lambda}(x)\psi_{n,c}^{(\alpha)}(y) \omega_{\alpha}(y)dy  }$ which are exactly given thanks to \eqref{Eq3.2}. Since $M_{s,\lambda}$ is an odd function , $C_{2n}(M_{s,\lambda}) = $ . Moreover
\begin{eqnarray}
C_{2n+1}(M_{s,\lambda}) &=& \sum_{\ell=0}^{\infty}\beta_{2\ell+1}^{2m+1} \sum_{k=0}^{\infty} \frac{1}{\lambda^{k(2-s)}} \int_{-1}^{1} \sin(\lambda^k x) \hat{P}^{(\alpha)}_{2\ell+1}(x)\omega_{\alpha}(x) dx \nonumber \\
&=& \sqrt{\pi} 2^{\alpha+\frac{1}{2}} \sum_{\ell=1}^{\infty} (-1)^{\ell} \beta_{2\ell+1}^{2m+1} \frac{\Gamma(2\ell+\alpha+3)}{\sqrt(h_{2\ell+1})\Gamma(2\ell+1)} \sum_{k=1}^{\infty} \lambda^{k(s-\alpha-5/2)} J_{2\ell + \alpha+\frac{3}{2}}(\lambda^k)
\end{eqnarray}
In figure \ref{WM} we have plotted the function $M_{1,2}$ and the graph of the error $ M_{1,2} - S_N(M_{1,2}(x)) $
